subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: All three printed formats implemented and measured. PRINTED PAGE RENDERED (licensed PDF p.762, ISO/IEC 1989:2023) and matched against specs/ISO_COBOL.md line-for-line: F1 `SUBTRACT {identifier-1|literal-1}... FROM {identifier-2 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F2 adds `FROM {identifier-2|literal-2}` + `GIVING {identifier-3 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F3 `{CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-4 FROM identifier-5 [rounded-phrase]`; each with the bracketed CHOICE-INDICATOR size-error group and `[END-SUBTRACT]`. Underlining measured off the render: ON is NOT underlined in either size-error line (optional word) and the grammar spells `ON? SIZE ERROR` once, in conditionalPhraseHead (CobolParserCore.g4), which the plain and the NOT phrase share. MEASURED (probe dir probe/subtract): p1 F1 multi-operand + multi-receiver + per-receiver ROUNDED; p2/g6 F2 with literal-2 and with several GIVING receivers each carrying its own ROUNDED; p3/p4/m3 F3 with both CORR and CORRESPONDING, ROUNDED after identifier-5, both size-error branches, END-SUBTRACT; g7 the REVERSED phrase order (5.2.6.4 choice indicators - zero or more, each at most once, any order); h5 END-SUBTRACT as a scope terminator inside IF; h1 the FROM sender as a data reference; g9/g10 a function-identifier in both sending positions (8.4.3.1.2 makes it an identifier). The format-mixing violations the union grammar admits are narrowed back at bind and REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME with COBOL1689: two FROM operands under GIVING (g1), ROUNDED on the F2 sending operand (g2), operands with no FROM (g3), a literal receiver in F1 (g4), GIVING with no FROM (g5), a function-identifier F1 receiver (g11). Verified at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (h2); ROUNDED MODE IS gates 2014+ (h3, COBOL0803 - 14.7.4's row, not this one). Additional spec-derived goldens touching this row: conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/optional_on_size_error (ON omittable, SUBTRACT leg), conformance:cases/14.9.26-MULTIPLY/pb134_giving_sending_operands (F2 one sending literal), conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/pb45_function_in_sending_operands (F2 function sender).
